ia-board-chair.summary: Your County Supervisor card names the supervisors, and in 45 of Iowa's 99 counties it now also says which one chairs the board. In the other 54 it cannot: nothing published there pairs a chair with a name.
ia-board-chair.why: No statewide publisher records the chair, so it comes from each county's own board page or its own minutes — and most counties name it on neither, refuse this app outright, or word it too loosely for any reading to be safe to ship.
ia-board-chair.wanted: A county board page or set of minutes that names the chair beside the member, or a statewide list carrying a chair column — the supervisors' own association directory names every member and would need only that one field.

ia-municipal-officeholders.summary: The City card names your city and nothing else — not your mayor, not your council, not your clerk. That is true in 819 of Iowa's 939 cities. The other 120 are the 14 largest, 102 their county publishes and 4 small ones.
ia-municipal-officeholders.why: No one publishes Iowa's city officeholders in one place, and the cities do not publish alike: two in five have no website at all. Ten counties publish every city inside them, and the largest cities publish their own council pages.
ia-municipal-officeholders.wanted: A city's own council page, or one of the counties whose own page this project has not been able to reach. Best of all, one statewide list of Iowa's city clerks — the shape Wisconsin's Elections Commission supplies for its municipalities.

ia-polling-places.summary: Your precinct card names your precinct and cannot tell you where to vote in it. The state does publish every polling place in Iowa — but nothing published says which precinct each one serves.
ia-polling-places.why: The two things needed exist in different files. Everything that says which precinct a place serves is two years old; the current list dropped that column, so nothing joins it to a precinct without going through a stale map.
ia-polling-places.wanted: The precinct name carried alongside each polling place in the current file, as the previous edition carried it — one column, and the card could name your polling place. Failing that, any published pairing of precinct to place.

ia-supervisor-count-disagrees.summary: In Wright County your supervisor card names the county and no supervisors. Two state sources disagree about how many seats the board has, so nothing here can say who fills them.
ia-supervisor-count-disagrees.why: The statewide directory lists five supervisors where the state's own district map draws three. The map is the stale half here, and naming five people against a three-district map would put a supervisor in a district the map does not draw.
ia-supervisor-count-disagrees.wanted: The state's supervisor-district map redrawn to the five districts the county elects from, or any county list that prints a district number beside each supervisor's name.

ia-supervisor-count-impossible.summary: In Pottawattamie County your supervisor card names the county and no supervisors. The directory this app reads gives the board a size Iowa law does not allow, so nothing here can say who sits on it.
ia-supervisor-count-impossible.why: Iowa law puts a board of supervisors at three members or five. The statewide directory lists six for this county, which makes that table stale rather than the board unusual, so the names beside it are not printed.
ia-supervisor-count-impossible.wanted: The county's own published list of its supervisors in a form this app is allowed to read, or a corrected statewide directory whose board size matches what the county itself reports.

ia-supervisor-district-seats.area: Black Hawk, Calhoun, Cass, Dickinson, Guthrie, Kossuth, Lee, Montgomery, Palo Alto and Worth Counties, Iowa
ia-supervisor-district-seats.summary: Your County Supervisor card shows the district you live in and names the people on the board, and cannot say which of them holds your district. That is true in 14 Iowa counties, all of which elect their supervisors by district.
ia-supervisor-district-seats.why: The statewide map draws each county's districts and records no supervisor against them; the directory that names the supervisors carries no district beside a name. Both halves are published and nothing joins them.
ia-supervisor-district-seats.wanted: Any list a county publishes that prints a district number beside a supervisor's name — a board page, a certified election summary, or a county directory that carries the district.

ia-township-officers.area: Iowa — the townships outside twelve counties
ia-township-officers.summary: Your township card names the township and, in twelve counties, its clerk and trustees. In the rest of Iowa it names nobody. Twelve counties publish 186 of roughly 1,600 townships.
ia-township-officers.why: Iowa has no statewide list of township officers, and the townships do not publish for themselves. Twelve counties publish the officers of every township inside them, which is where all the named ones come from.
ia-township-officers.wanted: Another county's own township page, or best of all one statewide list of Iowa's township clerks and trustees. Failing that, the election results each county certifies, which name the winners of these offices.

ia-tribal-government.area: Tama County, and the Iowa edges of two Nebraska reservations
ia-tribal-government.summary: No card names the tribal nation whose land you clicked on, or its government. The Meskwaki Settlement lies in Tama County, and two nations seated in Nebraska hold reservation land inside Iowa as well.
ia-tribal-government.why: Each nation publishes its own council, and its own election districts where it elects by district, on its own site. No state or federal source lists them together, so this app has no roster it could name anyone from.
ia-tribal-government.wanted: Each nation's own published list of its council members, and its district map where it elects by district.

johnson-county-supervisor-districts.summary: Johnson County's supervisor card names the county and says its districts are pending — it cannot yet tell you which of the five you live in.
johnson-county-supervisor-districts.why: The county adopted five districts for the November 2026 election but publishes them only as a printed map, and the statewide layer this app reads still carries the county under its older at-large form.
johnson-county-supervisor-districts.wanted: A map of the five districts the county can share as data, or a link to one — the way Black Hawk County publishes its own.

marion-council-roster.summary: Marion elects its council by ward, and its ward boundaries are already measured and ready — but no ward card ships, because nothing here can name the four members who hold those seats.
marion-council-roster.why: The city's own website refuses this app's requests outright, and every other publisher checked maps its wards without naming its council: the county draws the boundaries, and no directory carries the people.
marion-council-roster.wanted: A council page this app can reach, or the four ward members' names with the ward each holds — the boundary is already built, and the names are all that is missing.
